description.narrative: Stakeholder Effect: Increased access to SME finance: The proposed investment will enable NTB to expand lending to SMEs in Sri Lanka, where access to finance remains constrained by collateral requirements and information gaps. Improved SME access to finance is expected to stimulate firm growth, support employment, and contribute to Sri Lankas post-crisis economic recovery. Contribution to Market Creation: Competitiveness: Commercial banks in Sri Lanka have historically been reluctant to lend to SMEs, which are perceived as high-risk due to lack of immovable collateral and reliable financial records. The pandemic exacerbated this perceived risk profile by disproportionately impacting SMEs through reduced consumption. IFC anticipates that the Project will demonstrate the business case for reinitiating lending to SMEs in Sri Lanka. The Project is expected to strengthen competitiveness in Sri Lankas banking sector by demonstrating the financial viability of SME-centric lending models, encouraging peers to replicate and expand services to underserved segments, including SMEs.

The proposed Project consists of an investment package of up to US$70 million to Nations Trust Bank Limited (NTB or the Bank) through two facilities: (1) a four-year, US dollar-denominated, amortizing, senior, unsecured loan of up to US$50 million (IFC A Loan) and (2) an unfunded trade facility of up to US$20 million under IFCs Global Trade Finance Program (GTFP). The proceeds from the IFC A Loan will be used by NTB to on-lend to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), including women-owned SMEs (WSMEs) in Sri Lanka, which remain underserved and face significant financing gaps. The proposed GTFP facility will provide critical guarantee support to a leading player in Sri Lankas SME and trade finance sector, focusing on export/import-oriented SMEs in key priority areas. The proposed Project will support the recovery of small businesses, which were disproportionately affected by Sri Lankas triple crisesnamely, the Easter Bombings of 2019, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the 2022 sovereign default. As the countrys recovery strengthens, the proposed IFC investment is anticipated to enhance NTBs ability to support economic growth and job creation.
